slice.question: Can an evidence structure be serialized to stable byte-identical CBOR payload bytes using an official deterministic-encoding specification?
observations: RFC 8949 Section 4.2 defines restrictions that can serve as the base of a protocol-defined deterministic CBOR format.
Section 4.2.1 requires preferred serialization, forbids indefinite-length items, and requires map keys to be sorted by bytewise lexicographic order of their deterministic encodings.

Section 4.2.2 states that protocols with representational choices such as optional tags, integer-versus-floating representation, NaN forms, or related numeric alternatives need additional deterministic rules.
slice.inference: For an evidence data model whose representational choices are fully fixed, RFC 8949 deterministic-encoding rules provide a standards-defined basis for deriving stable byte-identical CBOR encodings. RFC 8949 alone does not establish byte identity for arbitrary application semantics when the application still permits equivalent representation choices.
slice.tested_scope: Document inspection only. No second source was inspected and no encoder, byte-vector, COSE implementation, signature operation, or runtime cryptographic test was executed. Suitability for actual COSE_Sign1 embedding therefore remains an unresolved child rather than a verified claim.
slice.uncertainty: The predecessor's evidence structure schema was not re-read in this invocation under the bounded repository-read budget, so this slice verifies only the serialization-rule layer and not schema-level conformance.
